conbody.p: If your Plug & charge (PnC) auto-billing charge doesn't proceed or fails while charging is in progress, check your PnC contract certificate for expiration and renewal.

li.p: When the certificate expires, automatic billing recharge will not proceed.

Turn off the Plug & charge (PnC) function and use an external payment method until the certificate status is verified. If automatic billing recharge fails 2 or more times, the 3rd recharge attempt is forcibly switched to an external payment method.

conbody.p: If your contract certificate for Plug & charge (PnC) charging has expired or been revoked, proceed to the next step.

li.p: Sign a new contract to issue or renew a certificate.
After connecting the charging connector, try Plug & charge charging once. The validity period and revocation status of the certificate are displayed on the charger, and charging fails.
Disconnect and reconnect the charging connector and try Plug & charge charging again. The certificate of the newly concluded contract is installed and Plug & charge charging proceeds normally.

note.p: When the payment method is automatically changed to an external payment method, proceed with one of the following steps to reset the Plug & charge (PnC) function and use the automatic charge billing function.

li.p: Recharge your vehicle using an external payment method. From the next charge, you can use the Plug & charge (PnC) automatic billing method again.

Disconnect the charging connector and close the charging door. Wait for at least approximately 1 minute with the vehicle in ON position Vehicle must be in READY mode. Afterwards, you can perform Plug & charge (PnC) charging.
Plug & charge (PnC) charging can be performed using other chargers that support the Plug & charge (PnC) function.
